cards.text: Friend, Jeremiah the prophet was just beaten and locked in the stocks on orders from Pashhur the priest (Jeremiah 20:1-3). Here, Jeremiah talks to the LORD, and he does NOT hold back. His first words: "You have deceived me, O LORD, and I was deceived."

cards.question: Jeremiah tells the LORD, "You have overcome me and prevailed." Then he says what his days are like. What does everyone do to him all day long?

cards.text: Every time Jeremiah speaks, he cries out about violence and destruction. Picture your whole job being the guy who stands up in EVERY meeting to say "it's getting worse."

cards.question: True or false: Jeremiah says the word of the LORD has brought him honor all day long.

cards.text: So Jeremiah tells the LORD what happens if he says, "I will not mention Him or speak any more in His name." Spoiler, baker: staying quiet doesn't go the way he hoped.

cards.question: When Jeremiah tries to stop speaking in the LORD's name, what does he say the LORD's message becomes?

answers.text: A fire burning in his heart

cards.question: True or false: When Jeremiah holds the LORD's message in, he's able to keep it there.

cards.text: Fire, shut up in his bones. Friend, I spent years shut up in a junk drawer, and the hottest thing in there was a dead battery bragging about how much charge it had left.
And Jeremiah says he's heard the whispering of many: "Terror is on every side! Report him; let us report him!"

cards.question: Jeremiah says some people are watching for him to fall. Who are they?
The people watching Jeremiah say perhaps he'll be ___, so they can prevail against him and take their vengeance.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah turns on one word: "But the LORD is with me like a fearsome warrior." Friend, in the drawer, my backup was a TWIST TIE.

cards.question: With the LORD with him like a fearsome warrior, what does Jeremiah say will happen to his persecutors?

answers.text: They will stumble and not prevail

cards.text: And their shame won't be the quick kind. Jeremiah says it will be "an everlasting disgrace that will never be forgotten."

cards.question: Jeremiah asks the LORD of Hosts, who examines the righteous, to let him see His vengeance on them, because he has committed his cause to Him. True or false: Jeremiah says the LORD sees the heart and mind.
Right after committing his cause to the LORD, what does Jeremiah call out?
Jeremiah says to praise the LORD because He rescues the life of the ___ from the hands of evildoers.

cards.text: Then, right after the praise, Jeremiah says, "Cursed be the day I was born!" Friend, the only time I swung that fast was when the drawer opened, I thought "THIS IS IT," and somebody just grabbed the tape.

cards.question: True or false: Jeremiah wants the day his mother bore him to be blessed.

cards.text: He keeps going. He curses the man who brought his father the news, saying, "A son is born to you."

cards.question: When that man told Jeremiah's father a son was born, what did the news bring his father?
Jeremiah wants the man who brought the birth news to be like something. What?

answers.text: A tree planted by the water
A watchman on a high wall

cards.text: He wants that man to hear an outcry in the morning and a battle cry at noon.

cards.question: True or false: Jeremiah curses that man because he did not kill Jeremiah in the womb.
Jeremiah ends with a question. Why did he come out of the womb to see only ___ and ___?

cards.text: And he asks why he came out only "to end my days in shame?" That's where Jeremiah's words stop, friend: honest, raw and right there in the Word.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "I will not mention Him or speak any more in His name.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 quotes "THIS IS IT", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 3 quotes "A son is born to you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "Jeremiah the prophet was just beaten and locked in the stocks" adds a time the text doesn't give. Jeremiah 20:3 says Pashhur released him the next day, and 20:7 doesn't say when Jeremiah spoke these words. "Just" also ties the lament to the beating, a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "Spoiler, baker: staying quiet doesn't go the way he hoped" tips off the next two choice cards. It rules out the wrong answers "A whisper he can ignore" and "A dream that fades away" on card 6. It also points to the answer on card 7, which asks whether Jeremiah can keep the message in.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "Doesn't go the way he hoped" states as fact that Jeremiah hoped for something. The text gives no such feeling, and the line doesn't mark it as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The joke's comparison doesn't share the verse's core action. Jeremiah 20:9 is about a fire held inside that he can't keep in. The joke plays on the words "shut up" and makes a bragging dead battery the "hottest" thing in the drawer, so it mixes literal heat with bragging. It doesn't click instantly. The card mostly repeats verse 9 after cards 6 and 7 already covered it.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The choice card carries the setup for verse 12 itself: the LORD of Hosts who examines the righteous, Jeremiah's request to see His vengeance, and committing his cause. No story card tells that beat first. The question also says "vengeance on them," which points back to the persecutors on an earlier card the baker can't see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The story card quotes "Cursed be the day I was born!" That gives away card 2, which asks whether Jeremiah wants the day his mother bore him to be blessed. It's the same line said two ways, so the answer is already on screen before the question.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "Jeremiah curses that man" points back to a card the baker can't see. The question never says who "that man" is: the man who brought Jeremiah's father the news of his birth.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Both right answers, trouble and sorrow, are the only negative words among the five. The baker can reason out that much. Which word goes in which blank depends only on the exact order of the BSB line, so placing them is a guess at wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
